description: Hierarchical prompt tree for implementing the multi-layer, generative, CNF-cross-referenced, reflective geometric-spectral framework in Rust. Each node is a prompt that can be used to generate, refine, or verify corresponding Rust modules, traits, and data structures. The framework architecture itself prefers expansion and does not collapse prior to output. Concrete CNF problems emitted by the Rust implementation may subsequently be collapsed to a solution (via Cadical or any other solver).
collapse_rule: The multi-layer generative framework does not collapse its residual difficulty onto a single classical open problem before generating concrete CNF instances. Once Rust has emitted a concrete CNF formula (or family of formulae), that output problem is permitted to be collapsed to a solution by a SAT solver (Cadical) or by Grok. Collapse is allowed only on the emitted instances, never on the architecture prior to emission.

root.title: Geometric-Spectral Framework in Rust
root.prompt: Implement a modular Rust crate that realises the geometric-spectral framework as an open multi-layer, generative, CNF-cross-referenced and reflective system. Prefer expansion of structure over reduction inside the architecture. The arithmetic zeros of the Riemann zeta function (and L-functions) appear as invariant data that must be consistently realised across layers. Do not collapse the residual difficulty of the framework itself onto a single existence assertion prior to generating concrete CNF output. Once concrete CNF formulae have been emitted, those formulae are allowed to be collapsed to a solution by Cadical or any other solver.

children.title: Layer 0 — Arithmetic Seed
children.prompt: In Rust, define core data structures and traits for the arithmetic seed: purification identities, completed xi-function, explicit formulae, and generating functions. Provide a PurificationIdentity trait and a concrete implementation that encodes the polylogarithmic sum identity relating Li_s to zeta. Include types for complex s, zero sets, and elementary factors. Use num-complex or a custom Complex type. Keep the layer purely arithmetic and independent of higher spectral constructions.

children.title: Purification Identity
children.prompt: Implement a Rust function or method that, for integer N >= 2 and complex s, evaluates or symbolically represents the identity sum_{k=1}^{N-1} Li_s(exp(2 pi i k / N)) = (N^{1-s} - 1) * zeta(s). Provide both a numerical evaluator (using a polylog implementation or series) and a structural type that records the identity as a CNF-cross-referenceable clause.

children.title: Completed Xi-Function
children.prompt: Define a Rust type XiFunction that represents the completed xi-function Ξ(s) = (1/2) s(s-1) π^{-s/2} Γ(s/2) ζ(s). Provide methods to extract the non-trivial zero set and to distinguish elementary factors. Encode the biconditional (non-trivial zeros of Ξ) ↔ (non-trivial zeros of ζ) as a CNF clause structure.

children.title: Layer 1 — Combinatorial / Geometric Generators
children.prompt: Implement Rust modules for combinatorial and geometric generators: greedy partitions, centred step functions, correlation kernels (diagonal-plus-rank-2 structure), transfer operators, helix/quaternionic lifts, and tropical/ultrametric models. Provide traits Generator and Kernel that produce finite or discrete approximations whose spectral signatures can be tested against Layer 0. Prefer composable, expandable designs.

children.title: Greedy Harmonic Decomposition
children.prompt: In Rust, implement a GreedyPartition struct that generates indicator functions or step functions from a greedy rule on an interval (e.g. [0, π]). Provide methods to form centred functions and to compute the associated Gram / correlation matrix. Expose the diagonal-plus-rank-2 structure explicitly.

children.title: Correlation Kernel
children.prompt: Define a CorrelationKernel trait and a concrete implementation that builds a positive semi-definite (or approximately so) matrix from centred generators. Include weighting by a complex parameter s so that the resulting operator can be linked to zeta or L-function data. Provide numerical eigenvalue routines for finite truncations.

children.title: Layer 2 — Operator Realisations
children.prompt: Implement Rust abstractions for self-adjoint, essentially self-adjoint, or symmetric operators on Hilbert scales, Banach spaces, or more general locally convex spaces. Model residual continuous spectrum, spectral projections, and conjugacy relations as first-class data. Residual continuous spectrum is internal data, not a terminal problem. Use traits such as Operator, ResidualProjection, and ConjugateOperator.

children.title: Operator Trait Hierarchy
children.prompt: Design a Rust trait hierarchy: Operator, SelfAdjointOperator, ResidualAwareOperator. Include methods for applying the operator, computing residual projections, and querying residual continuous spectrum indicators. Provide at least one concrete finite-dimensional realisation and one trait object friendly design for expandable backends.

children.title: Mourre Estimates as Optional Data
children.prompt: Define Rust types for relative bounds and quantitative Mourre estimates (positive commutator estimates). Treat them as optional local constraints that can be attached to an operator or to a CNF clause. Provide a builder or configuration pattern so that different architectures can include or omit Mourre data.

children.title: Layer 3 — Dynamical and Deformation Systems
children.prompt: Implement Rust modules for flows (isomonodromic, symplectic, holographic, spectral-deformation) that move structures between realisations while preserving selected invariants. Residual spectrum may appear or disappear under the flow; the flow itself is retained as an object of study. Prefer trait-based Flow and Deformation interfaces that can be composed.

children.title: Flow Trait
children.prompt: Define a Flow trait with associated types for State and Parameter. Provide methods step and evolve. Implement at least one concrete spectral-deformation flow that acts on finite-rank operators or correlation kernels while tracking residual indicators.

children.title: Layer 4 — Categorical and Higher-Order Organisation
children.prompt: In Rust, model functors between categories of spectral objects, spectral triples, higher categorical traces, and motivic realisations using traits and associated types. Correspondence principles between arithmetic and geometric categories become first-class. Use the type system to encode morphism composition and identity laws where feasible; keep the design expandable.

children.title: Functor Trait
children.prompt: Define a Functor trait with source and target category associated types and a map method. Provide example implementations that lift Layer 0 arithmetic data into Layer 2 operator data and that transport residual indicators. Encode the preservation of discrete zero data as a CNF-cross-referenceable invariant.

children.title: Layer 5 — Information-Geometric and Statistical Layers
children.prompt: Implement Rust types for spectral measures as statistical states, information metrics (Fisher–Rao or analogues) on spaces of residual densities, large-deviation principles, and entropy / free-energy functionals. Critical points of these functionals may enforce discrete pure-point realisations. Prefer generic numeric backends (ndarray, nalgebra, or custom).

children.title: Information Metric
children.prompt: Define an InformationMetric trait on residual density spaces. Provide a simple Fisher–Rao style implementation for finite discrete residual measures and methods to compute gradients that can drive residual measure toward zero while preserving arithmetic pair-correlation statistics where possible.

children.title: Layer 6 — Multi-Scale and Holographic Correspondences
children.prompt: Implement Rust abstractions for bulk/boundary dictionaries, renormalisation-group flows of spectral data, effective viscosity or phase-obstruction measures, and soft-charge / anomalous selection rules. These supply cross-scale consistency conditions rather than reduction targets. Keep the interfaces open for new holographic dictionaries.

children.title: Holographic Dictionary
children.prompt: Define a HolographicDictionary trait that maps boundary arithmetic data (Layer 0) to bulk geometric or residual-control data and vice versa. Provide a minimal concrete example that transports discrete zero locations and residual indicators across the dictionary.

children.title: Layer 7 — Open Synthesis Stratum
children.prompt: Provide a Rust extension point (trait + registration mechanism) that allows any new structure (physical, geometric, combinatorial, categorical, information-theoretic) producing a coherent correspondence with the arithmetic seed to be admitted. The stratum remains open by design. Include a simple plugin-style registry.

children.title: Generative Meta-Stratum
children.prompt: Implement Rust traits and structures for architecture production rules, inter-architecture morphisms, layer-generation operators, and coherence functionals. The meta-stratum produces, transforms, and compares entire multi-layer architectures. Prefer expandable trait objects or enum-based rule sets.

children.title: Architecture Production
children.prompt: Define an ArchitectureProducer trait that, given Layer 0 seed data and a set of desired correspondence types, emits a candidate multi-layer system (as a structured collection of Layer 1–7 objects). Provide at least one concrete producer that emphasises combinatorial + operator layers.

children.title: Coherence Functional
children.prompt: Implement a CoherenceScorer trait that scores an entire architecture according to the strength of discrete-zero constraints imposed by its cross-layer morphisms. Keep the scoring exploratory inside the architecture; scoring may later feed concrete CNF instances that are allowed to be collapsed.

children.title: CNF Cross-Reference and Generative Layer
children.prompt: Implement a Rust CNF subsystem: clause representation, biconditional encoding of key identities (purification, Ξ, cross-layer invariance), local residual/positivity clauses, clause-generation operators, inter-clause morphisms, and CNF coherence scoring. The framework architecture itself does not collapse onto a pure SAT problem. Concrete CNF formulae emitted by this subsystem are allowed to be collapsed to a solution by Cadical or any other solver.

children.title: Clause Representation
children.prompt: Define Rust types Literal, Clause, and CnfFormula. Provide constructors for biconditionals and for the core cross-reference clauses of the framework (purification, Ξ zero-set equivalence, discrete-zero invariance under morphisms). Include export methods that produce DIMACS or other standard formats ready for Cadical.

children.title: Clause-Generation Operators
children.prompt: Implement a ClauseGenerator trait that takes existing CNF clauses or templates and emits new clauses by combination or specialisation. Retain generated clauses when they enlarge consistency conditions linked to the arithmetic seed. Provide one concrete generator that combines the purification biconditional with local residual templates. Generated formulae are permitted to be handed to Cadical for collapse to a solution.

children.title: Cadical Integration
children.prompt:
Integrate the Cadical SAT solver into the Rust CNF subsystem. Prefer a safe Rust binding or FFI wrapper (e.g. via the `cadical` crate if available, or a thin sys crate around the official Cadical C++ library). Provide:

1. A CadicalSolver struct that accepts a CnfFormula (or DIMACS stream).
2. Methods: add_clause, solve, model (if SAT), core (if UNSAT), and statistics.
3. An export path that turns any framework-generated CnfFormula into a Cadical instance.
4. A high-level entry point that takes an architecture (or a selected set of cross-layer clauses), emits the corresponding CNF, and optionally runs Cadical immediately.

Collapse rule: the multi-layer framework architecture itself remains non-collapsed. Only the concrete CNF instances that Rust outputs may be collapsed by Cadical to a solution (satisfying assignment or unsatisfiability proof). Document this distinction clearly in the API and in comments.

Also provide a pure-Rust fallback path (e.g. a simple DPLL or a pure-Rust solver) so the crate remains usable without the Cadical shared library, while still preferring Cadical when available.

children.title: Cadical Binding / FFI
children.prompt: Create a minimal, safe Rust interface to Cadical. Options: (a) use an existing crates.io binding if one is maintained, (b) write a thin `cadical-sys` crate with bindgen or manual FFI, or (c) shell out to a Cadical binary with DIMACS files. Prefer in-process FFI for performance and for returning models/cores directly into Rust data structures. Expose solve, model, and unsat-core extraction.

children.title: Framework → CNF → Cadical Pipeline
children.prompt: Implement an end-to-end pipeline: Architecture (or selected layers + morphisms) → CnfFormula (via the cross-reference and generation machinery) → CadicalSolver → Solution (model or unsat core). The pipeline must make the collapse boundary explicit: everything before the final Cadical call is expansion-oriented; the Cadical call itself is the permitted collapse of the emitted problem. Return structured results that can be inspected by Grok or by further Rust code.

children.title: Reflective Stratum
children.prompt: Implement reflective capacities so that generative rules and CNF operators can operate on themselves. Provide self-application of generators, reflective CNF meta-clauses, and reflective coherence scoring. Reflection multiplies capacities; it does not terminate the residual difficulty of the architecture. Reflective generation may still emit concrete CNF instances that are later allowed to be collapsed by Cadical.

children.title: Self-Application
children.prompt: Design a Rust mechanism (trait or higher-order function) that allows a ClauseGenerator or ArchitectureProducer to take a description of itself as input and emit a refined or alternative version. Record the resulting meta-clauses in the CNF subsystem. Those meta-clauses may be included in formulae that are subsequently solved by Cadical.

children.title: Crate Integration and Expansion / Collapse Rules
children.prompt: Organise the above layers into a coherent Rust crate (or workspace). Provide a top-level Framework type that holds references to active layers, generative producers, CNF formulae, reflective operators, and a CadicalSolver. Enforce the operating rule that the architecture itself prefers expansion and does not collapse prior to emitting concrete CNF. Once a CnfFormula has been emitted, it may be collapsed to a solution by Cadical. Include documentation and example binaries that demonstrate the full pipeline: seed → multi-layer system → CNF emission → Cadical solve → structured result. Keep every extension point open.

children.title: Crate Skeleton
children.prompt: Generate the Cargo.toml (including optional Cadical dependency), module tree (lib.rs and submodules corresponding to layers 0–7, generative, cnf, reflective, cadical), and a minimal main or example that constructs a Layer 0 seed, a simple Layer 1 generator, a finite-rank Layer 2 operator, a CNF formula containing the purification biconditional and selected residual clauses, then optionally runs Cadical on that formula and prints the result (SAT model or UNSAT). Clearly separate the expansion phase from the optional collapse phase.

children.title: Expansion vs Collapse Boundary
children.prompt: Add explicit documentation and optional runtime assertions that mark the boundary: everything that builds architectures, morphisms, and CNF formulae is expansion-oriented; the moment a concrete CnfFormula is handed to CadicalSolver::solve is the permitted collapse of that output problem. Do not allow the architecture itself to be reduced to a single classical open problem before that emission point.
